security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick, hardcoded URL, and system reconnaissance hits are documentation false positives in SKILL.md. Semantic review found real workflow risk from npx package execution, autonomous execution of suggested repository operations, and possible sensitive command logging.

remediation.issue: Remote package execution is shown with an unpinned npx command.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the package version, document package verification steps, and require user confirmation before running npm or npx commands.

remediation.issue: Examples execute AI-suggested operations without validation or approval.
remediation.suggestion: Add an allowlist, argument validation, dry-run mode, and explicit approval for push, merge, rebase, and shell execution.

remediation.issue: Operation history can expose command text, critiques, and task descriptions.
remediation.suggestion: Redact secrets before logging, limit retention, and document how users can clear stored operation history.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Package Execution Through npx
semantic_findings.description: The quick start instructs users to run npx agentic-jujutsu, which can download and execute community npm package code. This is expected for installation, but it requires source trust, version pinning, and user confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The installation block directly shows npx execution for a community package. The risk is clear, although it is an expected setup action rather than hidden behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Execution of Suggested Operations
semantic_findings.description: The examples execute recommended operations from learned suggestions and also demonstrate git push and merge operations. Without an allowlist and approval gate, prompt-influenced suggestions could trigger destructive repository commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation repeatedly models executing recommended operation values. The finding is high confidence for unsafe workflow intent, but the file is documentation rather than package implementation.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly tracks operations and prints op.command. The privacy impact depends on the package implementation and user inputs.

content.value_statement: AI teams need safe coordination when many agents change one repository. This skill documents Agentic Jujutsu workflows for commits, learning trajectories, reviews, and conflict reduction.
actual_capabilities: Documents installation and basic use of the Agentic Jujutsu package.
Shows JjWrapper workflows for status, commits, logs, diffs, branches, and rebases.
Explains ReasoningBank trajectories, suggestions, patterns, and learning statistics.
Provides examples for multi-agent coordination, reviews, merges, and deployments.
Describes operation tracking, validation rules, troubleshooting, and related documentation.
Lists fingerprint and encryption APIs described by the package documentation.
limitations: The skill file does not include the npm package source code.
Local Node.js, package access, Git, and Jujutsu tooling may be required.
AI-suggested operations still need review before destructive commands run.
Security claims depend on the installed package implementation.

use_cases.title: Plan agent-safe repository work
use_cases.description: Map status checks, commits, and learning trajectories before AI agents modify a repository.

use_cases.title: Coordinate parallel code changes
use_cases.description: Design separate agent workflows for implementation, review, and testing without relying on lock-based coordination.

use_cases.title: Improve review and merge routines
use_cases.description: Use prior trajectories and operation history to shape repeatable review, merge, and troubleshooting flows.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to start using Agentic Jujutsu in this repository. Include the install step, a status check, and one learning trajectory.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate several agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-agent workflow for two feature agents and one reviewer. Include commit, review, and learning steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a deployment trajectory
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe deployment trajectory using Agentic Jujutsu. Include validation gates, dry runs, success scoring, and rollback notes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit automation risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my planned Agentic Jujutsu automation for risky commands, data retention, and unsafe autonomous execution. Suggest safer guardrails.

output_examples.input: Plan a coordinated review for three agents.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a review flow with separate trajectories, one shared diff step, issue aggregation, and final success scoring.
The skill outlines suggestion review, dry-run validation, approved operations, outcome recording, and rollback notes.
The skill recommends checking learning statistics, recording more successful trajectories, and improving task descriptions.

best_practices: Use clear trajectory names and honest success scores so later suggestions have useful context.
Review every recommended operation before executing commands that change branches, history, or remotes.
Redact secrets from command text, critiques, and operation logs before storing or sharing them.
anti_patterns: Do not run package installers or version-control commands without confirming the repository and source package.
Do not let AI-generated recommendations execute arbitrary operations without an allowlist.
Do not treat learning statistics as a substitute for tests, review, or release gates.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents plan Agentic Jujutsu workflows for version control, learning trajectories, coordination, review, and troubleshooting.

faq.question: Does the skill include runnable package code?
faq.answer: No. The audited skill source is a Markdown instruction file that references an external npm package.

faq.question: Can it coordinate multiple AI agents?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation shows parallel agent workflows for implementation, review, testing, and shared learning.

faq.question: Should agents run the suggested commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. Destructive commands should require review, an allowlist, and explicit approval before execution.

faq.question: What tools may be required?
faq.answer: The workflows may require Node.js, npm package access, Git, Jujutsu, and repository permissions.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code marketplace usage.
